value.name: Daniel warns about probate delay
value.description: Daniel explains that he cannot afford to wait six months for probate to drag on because other pressures are closing in on him.
evidence: nough that I cannot wait six months for probate to drag on.
I have a business partner who is about to discover something I would prefer he not discover.

value.name: Daniel reveals belief house was his
value.description: Daniel says he entered the situation believing the house belonged to him based on what his mother told him.
evidence: I came into this thinking the house was mine.
I have been told, by my mother, that the house was mine.

value.name: Daniel fears losing more than house
value.description: Daniel says that if a September document says the house is not his, he will lose more than the property itself.
evidence: If you tell me now that some piece of paper signed in September says otherwise, I am going to lose more than the house.

value.name: Asha confirms understanding
value.description: Asha responds that she understands Daniel's statement without taking his side.

value.name: Daniel denies being bad person
value.description: Daniel insists he is not a bad person, revealing his fear of being judged by others.

value.name: Daniel feels condemned by family
value.description: Daniel says Rosa and Lucia think badly of him and recalls his mother's love while defending her memory.
evidence: "Rosa thinks I am. Lucia thinks I am. They have always thought I was."
"My mother loved me. She did. She told me the house was mine."

value.name: Daniel accuses sister of influencing mother
value.description: Daniel suggests that his sister manipulated their sick mother into signing paperwork against his interests.
evidence: Whatever Rosa says she said in some room, whatever piece of paper she signed because she was sick and tired and being told what to do by my sister who was here every day whispering in her ear—

value.name: Asha refuses to take sides
value.description: Asha tells Daniel she cannot be on anyone's side because her role requires neutrality.
evidence: "I cannot be on anyone's side," Asha said, gently. "That is the job. If I am on someone's side, I am not doing the job."

value.name: Daniel asks Asha for support
value.description: Daniel asks Asha to help him in a way that will not destroy him.
evidence: "Then do the job in a way that does not destroy me."

value.name: Asha promises to find truth
value.description: Asha promises only to do the job by finding out the truth, noting that she made the same promise to Daniel's sister and owes it to his mother.
evidence: "I will do the job in a way that finds out the truth. That is the only promise I can make to you. It is the same promise I made to your sister. It is the same promise I owe your mother."

value.name: Daniel accepts verdict-like response
value.description: Daniel falls silent and nods once, reacting as if he has just heard a verdict.
evidence: He was quiet. Then he nodded, once, the way a man nods when he has heard a verdict.
